Since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\), \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), so it induces an integral ring isomorphism \[  ar\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r}, \qquad ar s_\lambda\mapsto ar s_{\lambda'}. \] For every \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), \[ i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'. \] Indeed, for \(i,j>0\), the left side says \(\lambda_a\ge i\) for \(1\le a\le j\), equivalently \(\lambda'_b=\#\{a:\lambda_a\ge b\}\ge j\) for \(1\le b\le i\), which is \(j^i\subseteq\lambda'\). If \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), both rectangles are empty and the equivalence is vacuous. Thus \( ar\omega_{r,q}\) maps the displayed \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_{r,q;i,j}\) bijectively to the displayed \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_{q,r;j,i}\). Therefore \[  oxed{ ar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}}. \] The missing basiswise interval-ideal certificate is established.
